Convert this existing Tailwind site so padding, gaps and font sizes scale with the viewport instead of jumping at sm/md/lg breakpoints. There are about 20 sections using .container and px values.
The site header is enormous on a 2560 monitor, the nav links look like headlines. The rest of the page scaling up is fine, just not the header.

Our full-height hero uses 100vh and on iPhone the bottom is hidden behind Safari's toolbar, and the headline font size changes while I scroll. The rest of the site uses viewport-based sizing from our design frame.

Use $fluid-design to set up a Vite + SCSS marketing page from our 1600x1000 desktop frame and 375 phone frame, with growth capped at 1.4x on large monitors.

Build a pinned section where scrolling scrubs through a product video frame by frame, then releases into the next section. We use Motion.
Make this pricing card grid responsive: one column on mobile, two on tablet, three on desktop, with the usual Tailwind sm/md/lg breakpoints. Nothing needs to scale continuously.
Generate a Utopia-style modular type scale with clamp(): a 1.2 ratio at 320px to 1.333 at 1240px, steps -2 to 5, as CSS custom properties for our blog.
Set up a colour system for our app: a brand ramp from 50 to 950, semantic surface/text/border tokens, and a dark theme toggled by a class on html.
Scaffold a React component library with Button, Input, Select and Dialog, using Radix primitives and Storybook, published as an npm package.
